title: Japan Golden Route: 7 Days — Tokyo, Kyoto & Osaka for First-Timers
description: The classic first-timer's journey through Japan — neon-lit Tokyo, ancient Kyoto temples, and Osaka's legendary street food scene, connected by bullet trains with Mt. Fuji views.

days.title: Arrive in Tokyo — Neon Nights
days.description: Land at Narita or Haneda, grab your Suica IC card, and dive straight into Tokyo's electric energy with an evening in Shibuya and Shinjuku.

activities.name: Arrive & Get Your Suica Card
activities.description: Pick up a Suica IC card (¥2,000 with ¥1,500 credit) at the airport station. Take the Narita Express (¥3,250, 60 min) or Keisei Skyliner (¥2,520, 36 min to Ueno) to central Tokyo. Head to the world's busiest pedestrian crossing around 5-7pm for golden hour. Watch 3,000 people scramble across every 90 seconds from the Starbucks window above, then cross it yourself. Visit the Hachiko statue while you're there.

activities.name: Golden Gai
activities.description: 200+ bars the size of wardrobes tucked into narrow alleys. Each seats 6-8 people. Pick one with an open seat, order whisky, and talk to whoever's next to you. Most charge a small cover (¥500-1,000).

days.title: Ancient Temples & Digital Art
days.description: From Tokyo's oldest temple at dawn to cutting-edge digital art — a day spanning centuries of Japanese culture.

activities.name: Senso-ji Temple
activities.description: Tokyo's oldest temple opens at 6am. Arrive before 8am for incense-filled halls with almost no one else around. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and browse Nakamise shopping street for traditional snacks and souvenirs.

activities.name: Akihabara (Electric Town)
activities.description: Multi-story electronics shops, retro gaming arcades, anime megastores, and maid cafés. Even if anime isn't your thing, the sensory overload is an experience in itself. Tokyo's most immersive digital art experience — rooms of projected flowers, light sculptures, and installations that respond to your movement. Book tickets online in advance.

activities.name: Sumida River Evening Walk
activities.description: Stroll along the river for night views of Tokyo Skytree lit up against the skyline.

days.title: Shrines, Street Style & Street Food
days.description: A forest shrine, kawaii fashion, the world's best fish market, and a sunset rooftop — Tokyo's range in a single day.

activities.name: Meiji Jingu Shrine
activities.description: A 170-acre forest in the heart of Tokyo. Walk through the towering torii gate and tree-lined gravel path — it feels like leaving the city entirely. The shrine grounds are free and beautifully maintained. Directly from Meiji Shrine, walk into Harajuku's sensory riot — crepe shops, kawaii fashion, and vintage stores. Cat Street (the parallel backstreet) has independent boutiques, specialty coffee, and street art.

activities.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
activities.description: The original wholesale market moved to Toyosu, but the outer market street food scene is still thriving. Tuna on a stick, fresh uni, tamago on rice, grilled scallops — graze your way through.

activities.name: Shibuya Sky Observation Deck
activities.description: 360° open-air rooftop views of Tokyo at golden hour. One of the best sunset spots in the city.

days.neighborhoods: Shinkansen · Fushimi Inari · Nishiki Market · Gion
days.title: Bullet Train to Kyoto — Torii Gates & Geisha District
days.description: Board the Shinkansen with Mt. Fuji views, walk through 10,000 vermillion gates, and explore Kyoto's atmospheric evening streets.

activities.name: Shinkansen to Kyoto
activities.description: Take the 7-8am Hikari from Tokyo Station (2h40m, ~¥14,000). Sit on the right side (seats E/D) for Mt. Fuji views about 45 minutes in. It's one of those moments that feels genuinely cinematic. 10,000 vermillion torii gates tunneling up a forested mountainside. 15 minutes by train from Kyoto Station (Nara/Inari line, ¥150). The full loop takes 2-3 hours, but push at least to the Yotsutsuji viewpoint (45 min) — most tourists turn back before it.

activities.name: Nishiki Market
activities.description: 'Kyoto's Kitchen' — a narrow 5-block covered arcade packed with food stalls. Try pickled vegetables, matcha everything, fresh mochi, and grilled seafood on sticks.

activities.name: Gion District at Dusk
activities.description: Walk Hanamikoji Street in the geisha district — you might spot a maiko (apprentice geisha) in full kimono heading to an evening engagement. Be respectful, don't chase or block them.

days.title: Golden Temple, Bamboo Forest & Mountain Views
days.description: Kyoto's greatest hits in one day — from gold-leaf reflections to towering bamboo to the wooden terrace overlooking the city.

activities.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
activities.description: The gold-leaf temple reflected in its mirror pond is one of Japan's most photographed sights. Arrive right when it opens (9am) to beat the tour buses. The surrounding gardens are worth a slow walk. Towering bamboo stalks create a natural tunnel that filters light beautifully. It's often packed, but walking through is still magical. Continue to Togetsukyo Bridge for mountain views.

activities.name: Kiyomizu-dera
activities.description: The massive wooden terrace juts out over a hillside with panoramic views. The approach through Higashiyama's narrow streets is lined with pottery shops, tea houses, and sweet shops.

activities.name: Ninenzaka & Sannenzaka
activities.description: Stone-paved lanes leading down from Kiyomizu — atmospheric shops, matcha ice cream, and traditional architecture. Gorgeous at dusk.

days.title: Nara's Deer & Osaka's Street Food
days.description: Morning with bowing deer and the Great Buddha, then south to Osaka for the best street food night of your life.

activities.name: Train to Nara
activities.description: Kintetsu line from Kyoto (35 min, ~¥760). Nara was Japan's first permanent capital and is home to 1,000+ wild deer that bow for crackers. The Great Buddha Hall houses a 15-meter bronze Buddha in the world's largest wooden building. The scale is genuinely jaw-dropping — photos don't do it justice.

activities.name: Train to Osaka
activities.description: Take the Kintetsu line from Nara to Osaka-Namba (70 min, ~¥970). Check into your hotel near Namba or Shinsaibashi.

activities.name: Dotonbori at Night
activities.description: This is what you came to Osaka for. The neon-lit canal street is Japan's greatest food spectacle. Just walk and eat — that's the entire plan.

days.neighborhoods: Osaka Castle · Shinsekai · Kuromon Market · Namba
days.title: Osaka — Castle, Retro Vibes & Final Feast
days.description: Samurai history, a 1950s neighborhood frozen in time, and one last epic food crawl before saying goodbye to Japan.

activities.name: Osaka Castle
activities.description: The reconstructed castle sits in a large park beautiful in cherry blossom season. The interior museum covers Osaka's samurai history with panoramic views from the top floor. Osaka's retro neighborhood frozen in the 1950s. Tsutenkaku Tower anchors the area, surrounded by kushikatsu restaurants and old-school game arcades. This is working-class Osaka at its most authentic.

activities.name: Kuromon Market
activities.description: 'Osaka's Kitchen' — fresh sashimi, grilled scallops, Kobe beef on a stick, uni, seasonal fruits. It's touristy but the quality is real.

activities.name: Umeda Sky Building (Optional)
activities.description: The floating garden observatory offers panoramic views, and the basement Takimi-Koji alley recreates a 1920s Osaka street with restaurants.

editorialSummary: The classic first-timer's journey through Japan — neon-lit Tokyo, ancient Kyoto temples, and Osaka's legendary street food scene, connected by bullet trains with Mt. Fuji views.
